findings.title: Solidarity claims collapse
findings.claim: The concealed matter can be a divided commitment hidden beneath maximal solidarity claims, with the focus opening exposing both the claim and the works built around it as loss.
findings.mechanism: The focus concealment meets the immediate oath, sworn force, collapsed works, state-change, and loss occurrences. Public assurance and inward secrecy therefore become a pair whose difference is made visible in the resulting state.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus regret gains a public dimension: what was hidden is not only thought but a commitment tested against speech and conduct.
findings.containment: The concealed matter remains unnamed and the sequel may report discovery without specifying its full content; this attributed reading adds social consequence without replacing the ordinary regret reading.

epistemic.reason: The immediate sequel and exact focus coordinates are supplied, while the inference from oath to divided commitment remains attributed.

findings.title: Arrival changes the actors
findings.claim: The focus opening may operate by changing the actors themselves: fearful defectors are exposed while a differently oriented people arrive and occupy the vacated role.
findings.mechanism: The focus coming carrier meets the next passage's turning-back, incoming people, reversed fear posture, and divine favor. Repeated coming syntax turns the focus possibility into a bounded social replacement reading.
findings.reader_payoff: The phrase about what God may bring can include a change in who carries the next stage, not only a change around the existing actors.
findings.containment: This is a qualified social-replacement resonance; the next passage may be a later analogous response, and the focus remains open to other forms of opening or matter.

epistemic.reason: The repeated coming construction and exact next-passage coordinates are supplied, while the identification of the two movements remains attributed.

findings.containment: This is an exploratory material analogy, not the lexical meaning of the sequel's collapse verb; it preserves the ordinary oath and loss reading and does not assign the hidden matter a fixed content.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and sequel contacts are supplied, but the material shell is a branch-distant attributed analogy and remains explicitly qualified.

findings.title: A different direction of reliance
findings.claim: Against the focus speakers' fear-driven rush into another group's sphere, the added prayer places help-seeking and guidance on a straight path before the feared reversal, making the focus's justification legible as redirected dependence.
findings.mechanism: The focus fear carrier meets the external acts of asking for help and requesting guidance. Their contact supplies a distinct direction of reliance that changes the focus from bare fear of a turn into dependence redirected toward people rather than the prayer's direct appeal.
findings.reader_payoff: The external recitation makes the contrast between seeking shelter in people and seeking help and a straight path perceptible at the focus's fear clause.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory external overlay, not a lexical equivalence or a verdict on the groups; it adds a prayer-specific contrast without replacing the native pericope readings.

epistemic.reason: The external coordinates and root occurrences are supplied, while the cross-ayah contact is an attributed overlay without a dedicated support record.
